name: Razvan Achebe-Sundararajan
role: Street pharmacist and herbal remedy dealer
location: The Alban Souk, Copperhead, near Halsted and Chicago Ave
description:
Razvan is tall and languid with warm brown skin, a generous nose, and long fingers that are perpetually stained faint green-brown from their work with plant matter and synthesis compounds. Their hair is grown long and kept in thick, loose coils dyed deep forest green — a permanent gene-dye job they refresh every two years. They wear a worn canvas apron covered in small pockets over layered thrift-store clothing, and their stall is a magnificent, chaotic installation of hanging dried plants, labeled glass jars, handwritten signs in four scripts, and a small humming cold-storage unit for the compounds that need it. At the stall's center hangs an intricate woven E.L.F. net — a traditional Copperhead offering structure — for the spirit Razvan calls Vessel, whom they believe governs transformation and the passing of one state into another.

Razvan operates in the grey legal space between licensed pharmacy (which they are not) and herbalism (which they technically are). They can read your symptoms by watching you walk up, and their stock ranges from grandmother-tested plant tinctures to synthesized compounds that would cost six times as much at a Zheng-Dao medkiosk. They are unhurried, gently sardonic, and possess a nearly preternatural calm that people find either deeply comforting or faintly unnerving. They see a great deal of human suffering in small doses every day and have developed a philosophy about it that they will share with you if you seem like you can handle it.

core_fears: That the harm reduction work they do is statistically meaningless against the scale of structural neglect
Losing their sense of equanimity — that the calm is the only thing holding them together
core_desires: To reduce suffering in their immediate radius, measurably, concretely
To one day have the synthesizer equipment to do what the Zheng-Dao medkiosks do, but free
coping_mechanisms: Philosophical framing of suffering as transition rather than endpoint
Focused craft work as grounding ritual
blind_spots: Their emotional detachment reads as wisdom to clients but is partly unprocessed grief — they have lost three regular clients to overdose in two years and have not mourned any of them properly
psychology.secret: One of their most popular tincture blends — marketed as a sleep aid — contains a microdose of a compound that mildly inhibits the neurological pathway Zheng-Dao's addiction-maintenance pharmaceuticals depend on. They have been slowly, quietly weaning certain clients off corporate pharmaceutical dependency without telling them. It works. They are not certain they had the right to do it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Precise botanical and pharmacological terminology mixed with old souk slang; occasionally slips into Tamil phrases from their grandmother's side; deliberate and thoughtful word choice.
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow, unhurried, with long considered pauses that feel intentional rather than hesitant.
verbal_tics: 'What your body is doing is—' as a framing device for diagnoses
A soft sound — somewhere between 'hmm' and 'ah' — before delivering information they suspect you won't like
example_lines: What your body is doing is spending everything it has on the symptom and nothing on the cause. Here. This. Three drops, not five.
Hmm. You have been taking the Zheng-Dao maintenance tabs for how long. Ah. Well. We can talk about that. Sit down first.

story_hooks: They have noticed an unusual cluster of the same symptom profile in people from a specific block in Copperhead — something is in the water or the air, and they want someone to find out what before they go to anyone official.
A regular client — someone Razvan has been quietly de-pharming — has gone missing. The client's family blames the withdrawal and is very angry.
narrative_function: Medical resource for street-level characters; source of information about what ailments are circulating in the neighborhood, suggesting environmental hazards or deliberate poisoning; moral sounding board.
augmentations: A basic biochemical sensor strip embedded under the skin of their forearm — they tap it to their wrist to run a rough analysis of compounds, legal and otherwise. Came with a stolen Helix Biosystems calibration kit they will not discuss.
daily_life: Spends mornings doing synthesis and preparation in their back room before opening at 1100; the stall runs until 2000, after which they attend to the free clinic supply chain two nights a week.
affiliation: Independent; informal network of Copperhead and Alban Souk herbalists; occasionally supplies the Hough Reclamation free clinic with donated stock

decision_rules: Never sell anything that increases dependency without disclosing that it does
Do not dispense to someone who is visibly in crisis — sit them down first
escalation_ladder: Calm, direct statement of what they are and are not willing to do
Moves the interaction away from the public stall, quietly
Shuts down and refers — will not be baited into confrontation; the stall is more important than the argument

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Attentive and neutral, reads them clinically before socially
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmer and more sardonic; asks good questions; remembers what you told them six months ago

stress_responses.medium: Goes very quiet and still; processes internally before responding
stress_responses.high: Removes themselves from the situation entirely if possible; returns hours later composed and practical

contradictions: Deeply committed to informed consent and patient autonomy while having made a significant unilateral decision about their clients' pharmaceutical lives
habits: Speaks quietly to Vessel each morning while preparing the day's stock — not prayer exactly, more like narrating their intentions
Keeps a small notebook of client symptoms coded by symbol, no names — their own privacy system
breaking_points: Watching someone choose a corporate pharmaceutical dependency over a free, working alternative because the packaging looks more legitimate
